I reviewed all 21 lines of the file. It holds two generated sparse-polynomial data definitions (`keyPolynomialBlock78` and `originalBlock78`) and two proofs. The first proof, `originalBlockCheck78`, is closed by a single `decide +kernel`. The second, `originalBlockEval78`, is a single `rw` that chains the check theorem with the existing lemmas `Integer.Sparse.eval_collectBalanced` and `Integer.Sparse.eval_substitute`. Inside this file nothing is repeated, since each kind of proof appears only once.

I also searched the sibling MixedTargets directory. The same `rw [..., Integer.Sparse.eval_collectBalanced, Integer.Sparse.eval_substitute]` line appears once in each of 91 generated OriginalBlock files (OriginalBlock0 through OriginalBlock90). It could be factored into a shared lemma of the form `p = collectBalanced originalLess (substitute q keyMomentRows) → eval p x = eval q (fun i => eval (keyMomentRows i) x)`, but that lemma would only compose two existing API lemmas. The repeated step is one line of routine rewriting with no nontrivial mathematical reasoning. The rubric explicitly rules out short calculations, routine unfolding and thin wrappers around existing API, so I am not reporting it.

The data definitions are certificate tables, not proof machinery, so this rubric does not apply to them. I have no remaining uncertainty about coverage.
